title: Atmosphere Unit Activities

duplicateReceipts.note: The later Slack PDF is byte-identical to the canonical source. Its source occurrence is retained, while the canonical Blob and completed analysis are reused.

routing.ruling: Reference, not curriculum. This is an eight-page consumable activity packet with a reference chart, a cut-and-assemble model, labeling, drawing, word-search, crossword, and fill-in practice. It contains neither a teaching philosophy nor a paced instructional sequence, so it fails the curriculum skill's decisive philosophy-and-sequence test.

layout.visualHierarchy: large activity title, one instruction block, then one dominant work area
layout.notes: Each child-facing page owns one task. Page 1 is a vertical distance chart of the five atmospheric layers. Page 2 turns the same nested structure into a cut-and-assemble model. Pages 3 and 4 shift to labeling, matching, drawing, and written characteristics. Pages 5 through 7 provide a word search, crossword, and fill-in review. The footer and restrained blue accent make the loose activities read as one packet even though the mechanics change page by page.

topics.note: The Atmosphere, ages 9 to 11. The packet defines the atmosphere, identifies its five major layers, locates weather in the troposphere, and teaches ozone protection and atmospheric composition.

difficulty.notes: The packet stays on one conceptual target while varying the response mode. The opening chart supplies layer names and distances before later pages ask the child to label, match, recall, and apply those facts. A word bank appears on the labeling page, but the crossword and fill-in review require more independent recall.

theming.appealDrivers: The nested cut-and-assemble atmosphere model turns invisible vertical scale into something the child can physically build. The packet also changes mechanics often enough to avoid eight pages of repeated recall while keeping one visual language throughout.
theming.notes: The subject itself supplies the visual interest: Earth, atmospheric bands, aircraft, meteors, auroras, and satellites. There are no decorative mascots or licensed characters.

printFormat.notes: All activity content remains legible without color. The blue accent helps the source but does not encode answers, and the line-art craft is intentionally suitable for coloring before assembly.

aboutness.notes: The text sidecar combines ordinary OCR with vision reads of the diagram-heavy cover and terms page. Subjects and identity facts below are backed by exact spans. Rock Your Homeschool is an identity entity, not a content subject.

recipeMatch.notes: unit-study-packet is the exact whole-item match: one science topic expressed through a reference poster, diagram work, craft, word search, crossword, and review. Page 2 is a direct cut-and-assemble-craft match because the child cuts nested atmospheric bands and builds the layered model. The other pages are already explicitly owned by the packet recipe, so no new format gap is manufactured from a one-off variation.

notes: Carolyng described this as one example of a unit study. The strongest reusable signal is not a new recipe, because Homa already owns the unit-study-packet and cut-and-assemble-craft patterns. It is confirmation that a compact upper-elementary packet can move from reference chart to tactile model to independent recall without changing topics.
